note: Fuzzer-controlled bytes are accepted as JavaScript input when they are not recognized as Hermes bytecode.
The raw input bytes are copied into a C++ string that becomes the script source.
A trailing NUL is appended before the string is wrapped as a JS source buffer.
The input bytes are converted into a Hermes string using the provided length.
Hermes must preserve the string length and contents correctly when converting between UTF-8 and internal string storage; the bug is a violated bounds/length safety obligation in this conversion path.
Converting a JS string back to UTF-8 reads past the intended 2-byte boundary and triggers the stack-buffer-overflow read.
